_description: HOMA reference bond lengths, R_opt and alpha, Table I (p71).
_read_from: a 320 dpi RENDER of krygowski1993.pdf page 2, not the text layer
_why_rendered: The text layer substitutes PLAUSIBLE characters rather than producing garbage. Measured on this paper: the title's pi renders as '%' ('%-Electron Systems'), 'J. Chem. Inf:' for 'Inf.', and Eq. 7 comes out as '(Y = ~([R(s) -R,,I2 + [R(d) -RoptI2)-'' -- readable as a shape and useless as a transcription. Every value below was read from the render.

_equations.HOMA: 1 - (1/n) * sum over bonds of alpha(type) * (R_opt(type) - R_i)**2
_equations._eq8_note: Eq. 8 is the multi-bond-type form: each bond contributes with the SAME weight, and n is every bond taken into consideration, not the count per type.
_equations.alpha: 2 / ((R_s - R_opt)**2 + (R_d - R_opt)**2)   -- Eq. 7, fixed by HOMA = 0 for the reference Kekule structure

_interpretation: 1 is a fully aromatic ring with all bonds at R_opt; 0 is the reference Kekule structure with alternating R_s and R_d. It is NOT bounded below -- a strongly bond-alternating or strained ring goes negative.

_deprecated.CC_alt: The paper's CCb row. Its own footnote i reads 'This parametrization had been used in older papers, and it is recommended now to use parameters CCa'. Shipped for provenance and NOT selectable -- see _internal_inconsistencies.

_internal_inconsistencies._what: The printed R_opt and alpha do not both follow from the printed R_s and R_d in every row. Checked against Eqs. 6 and 7 rather than assumed.
_internal_inconsistencies.CO: Eq. 6 on the printed R_s and R_d gives R_opt = 1.2670; the table prints 1.265. The printed alpha of 157.38 is consistent with the PRINTED 1.265, not with 1.2670, so the two printed columns agree with each other and the derivation disagrees with both. Reaching 1.265 needs R_s = 1.361 against a printed 1.367.
_internal_inconsistencies.CC_alt: Eq. 7 on the printed R_opt gives alpha = 99.51; the table prints 98.89. THIS IS THE ONLY ROW WHOSE ALPHA DOES NOT RECONCILE, and it is the row the paper's own footnote tells you not to use.
_internal_inconsistencies.CS: Eq. 6 gives 1.6763 against a printed 1.677 -- rounding, not a disagreement.
_internal_inconsistencies._what_ships: The PRINTED R_opt and alpha, because they are what the literature uses and because they are mutually consistent in every row except the deprecated one. The derivation is kept as a guard, with the two rows above named as known exceptions rather than silently tolerated.

_oracle.benzene: p73: 'values for benzene itself 0.969 for electron diffraction geometry, 0.979 for MW geometry, and 0.996 for X-ray geometry'. All three back-solve to real benzene C-C lengths under the CC row: 1.399, 1.397 and 1.392 Angstrom.
